title: Nonnegative Matrix Factorization in the Component-Wise L1 Norm for Sparse Data
summary: Nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) approximates a nonnegative matrix, X, by the product of two nonnegative factors, WH, where W has r columns and H has r rows. In this paper, we consider NMF using the component-wise L1 norm as the error measure (L1-NMF), which is suited for data corrupted by heavy-tailed noise, such as Laplace noise or salt and pepper noise, or in the presence of outliers. Our first contribution is an NP-hardness proof for L1-NMF, even when r=1, in contrast to the standard NMF that uses least squares.
